name: MSTC Ltd
title: MSTC Ltd - 542597 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: MSTC Q1 FY27 revenue from operations rose ~22% YoY to Rs 94.25 crore, with PAT up 31% to Rs 58.12 crore on a 69% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose about 22% YoY to Rs 94.25 crore, led by e-commerce revenue of Rs 89.49 crore (vs Rs 70.03 crore). The trading and marketing (110% BG model) segment was exited and revenue from it fell to zero, so segmental reporting stopped from this quarter. PAT rose 31% to Rs 58.12 crore, and the Mahindra JV (MMRPL) posted its first positive PBT in about four years. Management described the quarter as the highest Q1 e-commerce revenue and PBT/PAT since listing, with new verticals (EPR, TReDS, travel) still awaiting regulatory or government go-aheads.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 70.03 crore YoY; highest Q1 e-commerce revenue

segments.name: E-commerce (only reporting segment from Q1 FY27)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 89.49 crore vs Rs 70.03 crore. Scrap sales make up about 50-55% of e-commerce revenue; minerals/coal blocks and other platform, software and AMC services make up the rest.

segments.name: Trading and marketing (110% BG model)
segments.commentary: Exited in FY26; dues recovered and revenue fell to zero this quarter. Segmental reporting discontinued.

segments.name: Mahindra JV (MMRPL)
segments.commentary: Posted a positive PBT for the first time in about four years, a token amount (share ~Rs 10 lakh), driven by higher ELV feedstock inflows under EPR norms.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to sustain double-digit growth on average, with lumpy quarters expected; no specific quarterly growth guidance given.
Margins expected to average near current levels, but may come under pressure at higher volumes, per the CFO; the 60%+ margin is not guaranteed.
TReDS platform: internal target to operationalise within FY27, contingent on RBI approval; transaction fee is the primary revenue source; no revenue quantum projected.
EPR e-trading portal is ready and integrated; awaiting government notification. Initially 5 sectors, expanding to about 15.
Travel portal: B2B live for government/PSU use; B2C launch awaits IATA empanelment. Revenue expected to be selection-fee based and slow to build.
Dividend: policy guided by DIPAM minimum of the higher of 4% of net worth or 30% of PAT; FY26 dividend already declared and subject to AGM approval.
Management declined to quantify EPR revenue potential (analyst's ~Rs 400 crore estimate for 2030-31 was called premature).
capex_capacity: Asset-light model: new verticals are being added selectively, stabilised, then scaled.
Travel portal and TReDS built on existing infrastructure; management says cost to establish was low.
Coal and mineral exchange feasibility under study; no timeline or capex quantified.
Corporate office opened in New Delhi; pan-India operations expanded.
demand_pricing: Scrap is cyclical with steel sector pricing and volumes; management expects mineral-block sales to be sustainable but cannot say whether 20-25% growth will continue.
Gross trading volume (about Rs 23,900 crore in the quarter, per an analyst) is driven by mineral block output and can swing widely; management declined to guide on it.

Competition: multiple coal exchanges are expected under the government gazette, and IEX has announced one; MSTC says it has the credibility advantage. APR (EPR) exchange: MSTC said it is the only applicant so far.
Karnataka liquor-licence auction is a new client won via the Rajasthan reference; stickiness depends on process integrity and licence tenure (e.g., 3 years).
Scrap revenue is spread across about 3,000 sellers; private-sector clients (Tata, Reliance, Vedanta, ArcelorMittal) are a stated focus.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue share would MSTC get from the APR/EPR trading market (about $2 bn by 2030, CPCB 4% fee), and what is the cash balance use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the EOI for the fee split and did not quantify MSTC's share. The cash-balance question was about FY26, not Q1, and was not answered.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the ~20% e-commerce growth and is it sustainable over the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was driven by more mineral blocks and scrap plant sales. Minerals are seen as sustainable; scrap (about 50-55% of e-commerce revenue) is cyclical, so 20-25% growth cannot be assured. Management aims for a double-digit average over time.

qa_highlights.question: How will TReDS generate revenue and will it contribute in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Transaction fee is the primary revenue source, with other charges tied to clientele and traffic. Revenue is contingent on RBI clearance; internal target is operationalisation within FY27, with no revenue quantum given.

qa_highlights.question: What is holding up the EPR exchange go-ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: The portal is built and security-tested, and integrations are complete. Operations need a government notification, which is a policy decision with no predictable timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will large recyclers' direct EPR transfers route through the exchange, and is there a committed minimum volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Once live, all transactions are to be routed through the exchange per government intent. There is no minimum volume guarantee, though the EOI gives some indication.

qa_highlights.question: How many vehicles are routed through the Mahindra JV, and how does the JV affect profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes are picking up, but per-vehicle realisation matters more than traction. Management said the JV has already turned profitable this quarter, with more traction expected from policy and state incentives.

qa_highlights.question: Will IEX's coal exchange affect MSTC's volumes, and what is the revenue from coal?
qa_highlights.answer: Multiple exchanges are allowed under the gazette, and MSTC expects credibility to help. It is still evaluating feasibility; coal revenue is not reported separately as it varies with the auction schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Can the ~60%+ EBITDA margin be sustained with operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said margins should average near current levels, but may come under pressure at higher volumes. The CMD cautioned that very high growth is not sustainable over time.

qa_highlights.question: How do liquor-licence and other new clients compare on stickiness, and what is the client concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Stickiness comes from process integrity and robustness. The Karnataka mandate came via the Rajasthan reference, and licence tenure (e.g., 3 years) limits repeat events. Scrap comes from about 3,000 sellers, so concentration is low.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EPR revenue potential (analyst's ~Rs 400 crore for 2030-31) and how exclusive is MSTC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Rs 400 crore estimate premature and declined to speculate. MSTC said it is the only APR exchange applicant at this point.

risks_watch: RBI approval timing for TReDS, which gates any revenue and the FY27 operationalisation target.
Government notification for the EPR/APR exchange; timing is policy-driven and unpredictable, and CPCB has not committed minimum volumes.
Scrap revenue (about 50-55% of e-commerce) is cyclical with steel prices and volumes; growth above 20% is not assured.
Lumpy GTV and mineral block output; management declined to guide on quarterly GTV.
Competition from multiple coal exchanges under the gazette, including IEX's announced exchange; MSTC's coal auction volumes could be at risk once exchanges go live.
Margin pressure at higher volumes; the CFO said the 60%+ EBITDA margin will not be sustained as a given.
Sustainability of Mahindra JV profit, which is a token amount, and reliance on ELV feedstock inflows under EPR norms.
Travel portal B2C launch awaits IATA empanelment; monetisation is selection-fee based and expected to be slow.
key_quotes: Riding on the highest ever Q1 e-commerce revenue of Rs. 89.49 crores, this is the highest in the Q1 since your company was listed in 2019 March.
So, our aim is to maintain a double-digit number.
There is no minimum guarantee as such but government will ensure that these transactions happen through the exchange.
Nobody knows as to how many certificates are getting transacted, what is the value of the certificates, how it is operationalized, how it is authenticated.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q1 numbers and the pipeline, but cautious and often deferential on timing and revenue quantum for new verticals (EPR, TReDS, travel, coal exchange). Management repeatedly deferred to regulators and government and declined to put numbers on EPR revenue or GTV.
